thread:
Sam (PM): quick follow-up from today's all-hands — promised a concise clarification on mission focus, positioning, and immediate GTM asks. TL;DR: what's the single most important priority for the next 6 months?

Claire (CEO): Priority is clear: make inference predictable and affordable for dev teams. Two parallel tracks: 1) scale Hosted (ease + velocity), 2) expand Dedicated/DC for predictable latency and contracts. Private stays as the compliance path. Metric: cost-per-successful-request at our 99p latency SLO.

Ben (GTM): to be concrete — for mid-market customers, do we lead with Hosted trials or sell Dedicated commits?

Claire (CEO): start with Hosted trials to prove product value and SLOs. Move to Dedicated when they need throughput guarantees or contractual isolation. Sales playbook will include a migration checklist and benchmark doc.

Jorge (Head of Product): on positioning vs cloud-managed endpoints: emphasize our runtime optimizations (continuous batching, KV caching) and the unified control plane across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. Also call out cost levers (quantization profiles, smart routing) — that’s a practical differentiator.

Maya (Eng Lead): small nit — can we publish concise perf profiles per model+hw? sales asks for that.

Ruth (Research): we can add a short matrix: model family x accelerator x expected tokens/sec and tail latency at p50/p95. Will need infra samples though.

Jorge (Head of Product): agreed. Product will produce a 1-pager perf matrix + migration guide. Target: publish to the docs hub in 3 weeks.

Ben (GTM): competitive question — how do we frame against the big cloud providers who now offer managed LLM endpoints?

Claire (CEO): three angles: 1) predictability + unit economics (we give knobs that actually change cost in measurable ways), 2) deployment flexibility (same API across modes), 3) developer ergonomics (streaming, eval hooks, rollout policies). Don't lead with feature parity vs clouds — lead with operational economics and predictable latency.

Sam (PM): any quick words on pricing signals — committed discounts vs usage-based? what's leadership's expectation for new contracts?

Claire (CEO): hybrid pricing — continue usage-first for self-serve; promote committed/Dedicated for customers needing predictability. We want to measure: % revenue from committed vs usage. Short term: incentives for AE to propose committed deals when they cross throughput thresholds.

Maya (Eng Lead): operational ask — can we get a prioritized list of three infra features that unblock Dedicated sales? I think: autoscaling latency SLOs, per-tenant KV cache controls, and safer rollout fallbacks.

Claire (CEO): yes. Jorge take lead, Maya & Ruth to define acceptance criteria.

Jorge (Head of Product): will do. I'll spin up a working group. Planning doc + tracking board in 48h. Please add any customer asks to the board.

Ben (GTM): can we get a short playbook for a standard proof-of-concept (Hosted -> Dedicated path) so AEs don't hand-roll it? even a checklist helps.

Jorge (Head of Product): POC playbook is in scope for the working group. Expect a template + deck.

Ruth (Research): one more competitive note — open-source inference runtimes are improving fast. we should call out in docs where our kernel/optimizer differences matter (e.g., long-context attention, KV cache savings).

Claire (CEO): good point. Docs team: add a "why Redwood" technical appendix with benchmarks and edge cases. Ops-bot: remind docs owners in 24h.

ops-bot: Reminder set for #docs-team in 24 hours — follow up for "why Redwood" appendix.

Sam (PM): thanks all. Action items I heard: Jorge to create working group + board; Docs to publish perf matrix and "why Redwood" appendix; Product to draft POC playbook; Eng to list infra unblockers. I'll capture these and ping assignees. :thumbsup:

Claire (CEO): thanks — appreciate the focus. We'll re-check progress in the next all-hands. If anyone has specific deal/legal constraints or competitor intel to share, DM me or drop in the board.

Ben (GTM): copying a few customer asks into the board now.

Maya (Eng Lead): adding infra notes.

Jorge (Head of Product): created the board and the initial epic. link: https://rwd.internal/boards/INF-2026-POC (internal link)

Sam (PM): perfect — closing the thread. If you want to be on the working group, reply here or DM Jorge.

Claire (CEO): :rocket:
